questions.prompt: Why can a copy in one stream overlap a kernel in another?
options: Copies run on separate copy engines, so they don't compete with the compute engine
questions.explanation: Different hardware engines, different streams: real overlap.

questions.prompt: Copy in 10 µs, compute 4 µs, copy out 10 µs per batch, perfectly pipelined over many batches. Steady-state time per batch, in µs?
questions.explanation: The slowest engine sets the rate: max(10, 4, 10).

questions.prompt: Why don't more chunks always help?
options: Each copy and launch has a fixed cost, and tiny kernels stop filling the GPU
questions.explanation: Fill and drain shrink, but per-chunk overheads grow.

questions.prompt: What must host memory be for cudaMemcpyAsync to really be asynchronous?
questions.explanation: Pageable memory forces a staged, synchronous copy.

questions.prompt: In a ring all-reduce over g GPUs, how does the bandwidth term scale with g?
questions.explanation: Rings are bandwidth-optimal; the latency term is what grows.
